title: Generation of eGFP-ARF-P2A-TIR1 or ARF-HA-P2A-TIR1 Progenitor Cells
author: Kizhakke Mattada Sathyan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bde4i3gw
materials: Separate proteins by loading 10 µL of the samples on a 10 % acrylamide gel, transfer the proteins onto nitrocellulose or PVDF membrane, block membrane with 7.5 % nonfat dry milk, and probe with anti-GFP or anti-HA and anti-TIR1 antibodies. β-Actin (1:5000; Sigma, A1978) can be used as a loading control. Include parental cell lysate as a negative control (Figure 2C). After insertion and expression are confirmed by genomic PCR and Western blot, the construct should be sequenced to confirm that mutations were not incorporated during the process. This cell line will serve as the progenitor cell line for tagging genes of interest with full-length AID.

steps.title: Detach cells from dish
steps.instruction: Remove media, wash cells with PBS, add 0.5 mL of 0.05 % trypsin, incubate 2–3 min at room temperature, then rinse and collect cells with 10 mL fresh media.

steps.title: Remove trypsin and resuspend
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 500 × g for 5 min in a swinging‑bucket centrifuge, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL fresh media.

steps.title: Seed cells for transfection
steps.instruction: Plate 2.0–3 × 10⁵ cells per well of a six‑well plate to reach 30–40 % confluence the next day.

steps.title: Prepare transfection reagents
steps.instruction: Label two 1.5 mL tubes per well: one “DNA” and one “Lipofectamine”. Add 125 µL Opti‑MEM I reduced serum to each tube.

steps.title: Add lipofectamine and p3000
steps.instruction: To the “Lipofectamine” tube add 5 µL Lipofectamine 3000; to the “DNA” tube add 5 µL p3000 reagent.

steps.title: Mix DNA with p3000
steps.instruction: Add 1 µg AAVS1 sgRNA (Addgene #126582) and 1 µg either eGFP‑ARF‑P2A‑TIR1 (Addgene #129668) or ARF‑HA‑P2A‑TIR1 (Addgene #126582) plasmid to the p3000 tube, pipette up/down three times. Include a negative control transfection with parental vector pX458. If transfection efficiency is low, increase Lipofectamine 3000 and p3000 to 7.5 µL each.

steps.title: Combine lipofectamine with DNA
steps.instruction: Dropwise, slowly add the Lipofectamine mixture to the DNA/p3000 mixture (total ≈260 µL). Mix by pipetting up/down three times.

steps.title: Incubate complexes and add to cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the combined mixture at room temperature for 15 min, then add dropwise to the cells in a serpentine pattern.

steps.title: Distribute transfection mixture
steps.instruction: Rock the plate sideways four times and front‑to‑back four times (do not swirl) to evenly spread the reagent, then place the plate in the incubator.

steps.title: Replace media after 24 h
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours post‑transfection, replace the medium with fresh growth medium.

steps.title: Expand cells to 10 cm plates
steps.instruction: Forty‑eight hours post‑transfection, transfer each six‑well culture into a 10 cm dish containing 10 mL fresh media (as in steps 1–2). Expand multiple wells to obtain enough colonies.

steps.title: Begin puromycin selection
steps.instruction: Seventy‑two hours post‑transfection, add puromycin to a final concentration of 1 µg/mL. Use conditioned medium (8 : 2 ratio fresh : filtered cultured medium) to improve survival. If colonies are few, start selection at 120 h instead of 72 h.

steps.title: Refresh puromycin media after 3 d
steps.instruction: Three days into selection, replace with fresh medium containing 1 µg/mL puromycin and continue selection for two more days.

steps.title: Optional extended puromycin selection
steps.instruction: If many cells remain in the negative‑control well after five total days, replace with fresh puromycin medium and continue for two additional days (total seven days).

steps.title: Remove selection and grow colonies
steps.instruction: After 5–7 days of puromycin, all cells in the untransfected control should be dead. Remove selection medium, expand cells without puromycin, and allow colonies to appear (typically 2–3 weeks).

steps.title: Mark and identify GFP colonies
steps.instruction: Mark individual colonies on the bottom of the plate with a marker. For eGFP‑ARF‑P2A‑TIR1 cells, examine under a fluorescent microscope and select colonies with uniform nuclear GFP; for ARF‑HA‑P2A‑TIR1, select all colonies.

steps.title: Pick colonies with trypsin (hand)
steps.instruction: Using a P20 pipette set to 20 µL, aspirate ~10 µL of 0.05 % trypsin, dispense a small droplet onto a colony, scrape the colony with the tip while the droplet bridges plate and tip, aspirate the detached cells, and transfer the entire colony to a 96‑well plate. Resuspend in 200 µL media and move to a 24‑well plate containing 1 mL media per well.

steps.title: Pick colonies with cloning cylinders
steps.instruction: Autoclave silicone‑greased glass petri dish and forceps. Aspirate media from the plate, wash with PBS, tilt plate to pool PBS away, place a silicone‑greased cloning cylinder over the colony, add 20 µL trypsin, incubate at 37 °C until cells detach, resuspend in 100 µL media, and transfer to a 24‑well plate with 1 mL media.

steps.title: Passage picked colonies
steps.instruction: When colonies reach confluency, pipette up/down to detach cells, transfer 100 µL to a new plate with fresh media for continued passaging, and move the remaining ~0.9 mL to a 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Collect samples for DNA and protein
steps.instruction: Aliquot 100 µL of the 0.9 mL suspension into a fresh tube for genomic DNA isolation (keep on ice). Centrifuge the remaining ~0.8 mL at 6000 × g for 2 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare lysate for Western blot
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL 2× SDS (Laemmli) sample buffer to the cell pellet, mix thoroughly, then heat at 95 °C for 5 min, vortex 10 s, heat another 5 min, briefly centrifuge at 5000 × g, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Isolate genomic DNA (DNeasy kit)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 µL PBS, add 20 µL proteinase K, then add 200 µL Buffer AL and vortex. Incubate at 56 °C for 10 min, add 200 µL 100 % ethanol, vortex, transfer to a DNeasy Mini spin column in a 2 mL collection tube, spin at max speed (≈10 000–17 000 × g) for 1 min, discard flow‑through, wash with 500 µL Buffer AW1, spin, discard, wash with 500 µL Buffer AW2, spin 1 min, discard, spin again at max speed for 2 min, place column in a 1.5 mL tube, add 100 µL nuclease‑free water to the column centre, spin at 9000 × g for 2 min, then quantify DNA with a NanoDrop and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Perform genomic PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare a PCR master mix (components per kit) for the required number of reactions. Aliquot 20 µL master mix into each 0.2 mL PCR tube, add 5 µL of 10 ng/µL genomic DNA (use parental HEK293T DNA as negative control). Use primers: AAVS1GenomicF 5'-CTGCCGTCTCTCTCCTGAGT-3', AAVS1GenomicR 5'-ACAGTTGGAGGAGAATCCACC-3', and Internal R2 5'-ATTATGATCTAGAGTCGCGGC-3'. PCR cycling: 95 °C 5 min; 30 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 59 °C 30 s, 68 °C 7 min; final extension 68 °C 10 min; hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Run agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 % agarose gel in 1× TAE buffer, add 5 µL 6× DNA loading dye to each PCR tube, load samples, and run at constant 90 V for 1 h.

steps.title: Stain and visualize PCR products
steps.instruction: Stain the gel with SYBR Safe diluted 1:10 000 in 1× TAE for 10 min, then wash twice with 1× TAE for 10 min each. Visualize bands under a UV transilluminator. Expected sizes: 1892 bp (negative control), 7256 bp (homozygous integration), both 1892 bp and 7256 bp (heterozygous), and 4677 bp only with internal primer in integrated cells.

steps.title: Re‑heat protein lysate for blotting
steps.instruction: Thaw the frozen protein lysate (from step 21) and heat again at 95 °C for 3–5 min before loading for Western blot.
